pages.text: "I don't like peas!" Nils the little bear pushed green peas to one side of his plate. He ate only bread and potatoes. "After this, I'll play in the garden!"
Grandpa Bruno looked at the plate. "Peas?" "I won't eat them. They look bad." Nils raced to the garden. Summer sun blazed down.
But after a few rounds, his paws drooped. Every vine reached upward, while Nils alone crouched between beds. Paws on both knees, head down. "Why am I like this today?"
Grandpa walked between vine rows with a basket. "Remember this row?" Plump pods hung on green vines.
"Where you buried seeds one by one in spring." Grandpa picked a pod for him. Nils opened it. Five green peas in a row—the ones he had pushed away!
"I planted these?" Both ears perked. Grandpa nodded. "Your watering helped them grow this much." Nils gulped.
He popped one pea in and pressed with his front teeth. Crunch! "Oh! Chewing makes sweet juice come out!" Two more, three more. "Peas I planted—yum!" The pod emptied.
Strength returned to his drooping paws. Nils hopped around the garden. Pods filled the basket. "Grandpa, I'll eat all these tonight!"
At dinner, Nils called first. "One, a pea I planted first! Two, a bite of other food too! Three, clear the plate!" Both paws high! "Peas I planted—yum!"
Grandpa held Nils's cheeks in both palms. One bite tells you the taste, even if it looks unappealing. "Peas I planted—yum! Tomorrow I'll plant carrots!" Nils showed his empty plate.
